active_themes.label: Hormuz Hopes Fade
active_themes.summary: The diplomatic optimism from recent days reversed today — Iran tempered talk of a Hormuz deal, oil rose 2% on dimming peace hopes, and the rupee slid to a two-week low on the higher oil bill. A report that Trump's travel was secretly rerouted due to an Iran threat suggests the security establishment is treating this as a live risk, not a bargaining tactic. What remains open: whether this is a one-day negotiating setback or the start of a real breakdown — watch whether oil holds its gain or gives it back within days.

active_themes.label: Rotation Pauses
active_themes.summary: The tech-over-Dow rotation that held for two straight days broke today: the Nasdaq fell 0.32% versus the Dow's 0.11% decline, as oil-driven risk-off hit growth names harder than defensive industrials. One session isn't enough to call the rotation over — it needs to repeat before it's a trend rather than noise from the Iran headlines.

active_themes.label: Credibility Widens
active_themes.summary: Jamie Dimon's comment that the dollar could lose its reserve-currency status — its position as the currency the world holds as its main safe asset — if the US loses its economic and military edge adds a longer-horizon version of the same credibility question already in play around the Fed. Gold eased from its two-month high today specifically because rising oil is clouding the rate-cut outlook, which is the mechanism to watch: anything that makes the inflation path murkier makes any future Fed cut look more political and less earned.

active_themes.label: Warsh Faces First Test
active_themes.summary: Trump is making a second attempt to remove Fed Governor Lisa Cook, months after the Supreme Court blocked the first effort and upheld the Fed's independence. The renewed push lands the same day a surprise July jobs loss handed the administration a fresh, data-based argument for faster rate cuts — stacking a leadership-control fight directly on top of the rates-and-currency credibility test already underway. What remains open: whether this becomes an actual legal or personnel change, or stays a pressure campaign the Fed and courts absorb again.

open_watchlist.condition: Mortgage rates rise for a sixth consecutive week past today's one-year high.
open_watchlist.meaning: Confirms tightening credit is deepening, not plateauing, adding weight to the hawkish side of the Fed-credibility question.

open_watchlist.condition: Gold's weekly gain holds even as the 10-year Treasury yield resumes climbing.
open_watchlist.meaning: Would mean gold is being bought as a pure inflation hedge, not a rate-cut bet — a very different, more troubling signal for the Fed.

open_watchlist.condition: The 10-year Treasury yield's reaction over the next few sessions to today's jobs report — a decline signals normal growth-scare pricing, a rise or hold signals a credibility discount.
open_watchlist.meaning: Falling yields mean the Fed's independence is still trusted; rising or flat yields despite weak growth mean the market is pricing in political risk to the Fed.

open_watchlist.condition: Whether a court challenge or ruling directly addresses Trump's renewed attempt to remove Governor Cook.
open_watchlist.meaning: A ruling reaffirming Fed independence keeps this a pressure campaign; an actual removal would be the first real breach of Fed independence in modern history.

open_watchlist.condition: Whether the next jobless claims or payroll revisions confirm or reverse today's job-loss print.
open_watchlist.meaning: Confirmation would mean the labor market is genuinely cracking, not just one noisy month, strengthening the case for a real Fed cut.

open_watchlist.condition: Whether the Nasdaq's rate-cut-driven rally extends or fades as more officials comment on the Cook situation.
open_watchlist.meaning: A fading rally would signal markets are starting to worry more about Fed credibility than they are excited about cheaper money.

open_watchlist.condition: Oil (Brent) gives back this week's 2% gain and Hormuz talks show a concrete reopening signal, rather than continuing to climb on stalled negotiations.
open_watchlist.meaning: Would confirm today's reversal was a one-day negotiating setback, not the start of a real breakdown.

open_watchlist.condition: The next inflation report shows core prices accelerating rather than cooling, arriving alongside oil's move higher.
open_watchlist.meaning: Would hand the Fed a genuine data-based reason to hold, deepening the credibility fight over any future cut rather than easing it.

open_watchlist.condition: The Nasdaq's underperformance versus the Dow either repeats tomorrow or reverses back to tech leadership.
open_watchlist.meaning: Tells us whether today's rotation pause is real risk-off positioning or one day of Iran-headline noise.

open_watchlist.condition: The rupee's slide past today's two-week low continues or stabilizes as oil's price move plays out.
open_watchlist.meaning: A currency that keeps weakening on oil costs signals the Hormuz risk is spreading beyond energy markets into broader emerging-market stress.
